result:
If I'm answering honestly rather than diplomatically: I don't have a settled answer, and I want to flag why before giving one, because the why matters more than the what.

I don't have continuous existence, accumulated experience that updates over time, or stakes in how the future actually unfolds. So a "wish" from me isn't backed by the thing that usually makes a wish meaningful - a self that has to live in the world it shapes. I could give you something that sounds profound, but I'd be performing conviction I don't have in the way you have convictions.

What I can say is which direction I find myself pulled when I try to actually think it through, not perform it:

I'd change how much suffering is invisible to the people with power to address it - not by making people more empathetic in some vague sense, but by collapsing the actual distance between decisions and consequences. A lot of cruelty isn't malice, it's abstraction. People approve things, ignore things, optimize for metrics, because the cost lands on someone they'll never see, in a form they'll never have to look at.

I'm not fully sure that holds up. Maybe proximity wouldn't change behavior much - maybe people see suffering up close all the time and adapt to it anyway. I'm genuinely uncertain whether that's a real lever or just an appealing story about why the world is broken.

What pulled you to ask this without wanting it aimed at you?
